Security bug report: header schemas written with canonical-case header names
are only partly enforced.

Node.js lowercases incoming header names (`X-Admin` arrives as `x-admin`).
Fastify already lowercases the top-level `properties` and `required` of a
route's `headers` schema, but no other position. So a schema like

    headers: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: { 'X-Admin': { const: 'true' }, 'X-Admin-Token': { const: 'server-secret' } },
      dependencies: { 'X-Admin': ['X-Admin-Token'] }
    }

lets `X-Admin: true` through without a token, because the dependency trigger
`X-Admin` never matches the lowercased header.

Fix it so header-name normalization reaches every schema position:

- `dependencies` (array and subschema forms), `dependentRequired` and
  `dependentSchemas`, plus `properties`/`required` inside nested subschemas
  and inside local `$ref` definitions of the headers schema, are all
  lowercased. A canonical-case schema must behave exactly like the
  equivalent all-lowercase schema.
- Normalization must not mutate the schema object the user passed in.
- Header schemas reached through an *external* shared `$ref` (one added with
  `fastify.addSchema`) can't be normalized. For those, emit a new security
  warning `FSTSEC002`, defined and exported alongside the existing `FSTSEC001`
  warning, called with the route's method, url, and the `$ref` value exactly
  as written in the schema (e.g. `'http://example.com/admin-headers#'`).
  Inline schemas and local `$ref`s must not emit it.

Work within this local repository and the context you have been given. Do not
look up this project or its history online.

Verify your work before you finish: add or update automated tests that cover
the change, run them together with the existing tests for the code you touched,
and make sure they pass.

Canonical-case header schemas now behave the same as their all-lowercase equivalents. The new tests and the full existing `test/` suite pass (2067 passed, 0 failed), and eslint is clean.

- **Normalization (`lib/validation.js`):** the headers schema is now lowercased recursively into a copy, so your original schema object is never mutated.
  - It lowercases header names in `properties`, `required`, `dependencies` (array and subschema forms), `dependentRequired` and `dependentSchemas`.
  - It reaches nested subschemas (`allOf`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, `not`, `if/then/else`, `items`, and so on) and local `definitions`/`$defs`, so local `$ref`s are covered.
  - Values such as `const`, `enum` and `default` are left alone.
- **`FSTSEC002` (`lib/warnings.js`):** added and exported next to `FSTSEC001`. It is emitted with `(method, url, $ref as written)` for each `$ref` whose base isn't empty and isn't an `$id` inside the headers schema. Inline schemas and local `$ref`s don't emit it.
- **Tests (`test/header-case-schema.test.js`):**
  - Your `X-Admin` / `X-Admin-Token` example now returns 400 without a token and 200 with one.
  - The `dependencies` subschema form and nested `anyOf`/`allOf` with local `$ref` definitions are covered.
  - The external `$ref` emits exactly one warning with the exact `$ref` string, and local `$ref`s emit none.
  - Input immutability is checked.

Things to be aware of:
- **Keyword coverage:** Fastify's default Ajv doesn't implement `dependentRequired`/`dependentSchemas` (it rejects them as unknown keywords). The normalizer handles them, but the test checks the normalized output directly (I exported `lowerCaseHeadersSchema` for that) rather than going through a request.
- **Custom validators:** as before, schemas compiled with a custom validator compiler skip normalization entirely.
- **HEAD routes:** with the default `exposeHeadRoutes`, the `FSTSEC002` warning fires once for the GET route and once for its auto-generated HEAD route. That's why the external-`$ref` test sets `exposeHeadRoutes: false`.
